## Summary

Top-ranked Computer Engineering student at Unicamp (1st of 102), focused on LLMs and machine learning. Works across LLM research, multi-agent systems, and software development, combining strong technical skills with a history of academic awards and impactful projects. Self-driven and disciplined, motivated by building technologies that create real value and push the boundaries of what's possible. Current professional focus areas include agentic AI pipelines, knowledge graphs, Graph-RAG, and MCP-based tooling.

## Professional Experience

### Valor Capital Group | AI Engineer, Tech Summer | Jun 2026 - Present | San Francisco, CA
Selected as part of an elite cohort of engineers for the Tech Summer program (San Francisco and São Paulo), working directly with the Head of AI to build systems and infrastructure for venture operations and investment analysis.

- **Agentic workflows:** designing and deploying autonomous agentic systems to streamline internal firm operations
- **Data & intelligence layers:** developing data pipelines and intelligence infrastructure to support investment decision-making
- **Technical diligence:** evaluating the technical stack, architecture, and scalability of early and growth-stage technology startups
- Day-to-day work spans agentic AI pipelines, knowledge graphs, and MCP-based tooling

### Instituto Kunumi (kunuminst COLABS) | AI Researcher | Aug 2025 - Aug 2026 | Campinas, Brazil
One-year undergraduate research position.

- Research on the **automatic generation of Knowledge Graphs** and new techniques for **Graph-RAG** systems
- Developing pipelines for entity/relation extraction and prototypes for Graph-RAG-based question answering

### Enter | AI Fellow | Mar 2026 - Jun 2026 | São Paulo, Brazil
Selected for the AI Fellowship at Enter, the **largest AI startup in Latin America and a $1.2B unicorn**; a highly selective program designed to bridge advanced AI research and production-grade enterprise software engineering.

- Architected and deployed a **distributed, asynchronous, and concurrent web pipeline** using **FastAPI, Hatchet, React, and LLMs**, transforming a local script into a resilient, production-grade system that processed **thousands of judicial decisions**
- Developed a **novel automated framework for the continuous evolution of enterprise argument taxonomies** using text embeddings and LLMs, enabling dynamic and scalable knowledge discovery
- Shifted engineering focus from isolated model training to robust backend infrastructure: system architecture boundaries, high-concurrency execution, and deployment pipelines
- Featured on Enter's blog: https://www.blog.getenter.ai/en/posts/ai-fellowship

### XP Inc. | Machine Learning Summer Intern | Jan 2026 - Feb 2026 | São Paulo, Brazil
High-impact 4-week Summer Internship focused on mitigating customer churn in the High-Net-Worth (HNW) segment.

- Defined an operational churn metric and built a robust dataset consolidating dozens of features across registration, suitability, digital engagement, and macroeconomic indicators
- Developed a predictive MVP with **XGBoost**, selected after benchmarking against CatBoost and LightGBM; applied **STL decomposition** (Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS) to analyze temporal patterns and reduce noise
- Conducted rigorous feature selection and temporal feature engineering (max/min, trend, amplitude) to capture shifts in investor behavior
- Validated results through **Out-of-Sample (OOS) and Out-of-Time (OOT)** testing; potential retention impact quantified in the **hundreds of millions of BRL**

### MBZUAI (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence) | UGRIP Research Intern | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025 | Abu Dhabi, UAE

- Selected among the **top 3% of 2,000+ international applicants** for UGRIP 2025, a fully funded AI research program
- Collaborated on a complete AI pipeline for **multimodal 3D brain tumor segmentation, missing-modality synthesis (latent diffusion), and tumor response classification**, contributing to the BraTS 2025 Challenge under the supervision of Dr. Mohammad Yaqub
- Served as one of the final presenters; the team received the **Best Team Award** (top group out of 15)
- **Authored 3 papers** (1 as co-first author, 2 as co-author) on medical imaging and tumor-response modelling

### Semantix AI | Research Fellow / AI Researcher | Mar 2024 - Aug 2025 | Campinas, Brazil

- Designed, developed, and led **STELLAR** (Structured, Trustworthy, and Explainable LLM-Led Architecture for Reliable Customer Support): a production-ready LLM architecture built as a **Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)** of nine specialized modules and eleven predefined workflows, integrating few-shot classification, **RAG**, sentiment analysis, urgency-aware human escalation, compliance verification, user interaction validation, and semi-automated knowledge base refinement. **Published in the Journal of the Brazilian Computer Society**
- Built a **hallucination benchmark evaluating 7 models across 90,000+ questions** in English and Portuguese
- Researched and implemented advanced RAG techniques; engineered specialized data pipelines for RAG-based retrieval, enhancing customer support workflows

### Hyundai Motor Company | Data Analysis & Machine Learning Summer Intern | Jan 2025 - Feb 2025 | São Paulo, Brazil
7-week Data Science program analyzing complex market data to predict trends and identify sales opportunities.

- Enhanced the lead segmentation/conversion ML model, **boosting the F1 score from 21% to 39%** while enabling dynamic targeting
- Designed a deterministic algorithm to scale predictions across larger datasets, enhancing marketing efficiency
- Created a recommendation system for car models/versions based on purchase history and financial profile, boosting repurchase rates
- **Cut monthly data processing time from 3 days to 3 minutes** by automating data aggregation and visualization pipelines, preventing manual errors

## Research & Publications

**Profiles:** [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&authuser=2&user=ieyEKR4AAAAJ) | [ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Matheus-Ferracciu-Scatolin) | [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0009-0003-2014-356X)

### 1. STELLAR: A Structured, Trustworthy, and Explainable LLM-Led Architecture for Reliable Customer Support (First author)
Scatolin, M. F., & Pedrini, H. (2026). *Journal of the Brazilian Computer Society*, 32(1), 128-144. The journal is Qualis A2 and Scopus-indexed.

- Novel architectural blueprint for reliable, explainable LLM-based customer support: DAG structure, nine specialized modules, eleven predefined workflows, RAG, compliance checks, and human-in-the-loop escalation
- DOI: https://doi.org/10.5753/jbcs.2026.6044
- Paper page: https://journals-sol.sbc.org.br/index.php/jbcs/article/view/6044

### 2. Predicting Brain Tumor Response to Therapy using a Hybrid Deep Learning and Radiomics Approach (Co-first author)
Tikhonov, D., Scatolin, M., Banerjee, M., Ji, Q., Jaheen, A., Salem, M., Elsayed, A., Wang, H., Hashmi, S., & Yaqub, M. (2025). Submitted to the BraTS-Lighthouse 2025 Challenge (MICCAI 2025).

- Hybrid framework fusing fine-tuned ResNet-18 deep features with 4,800+ radiomic and clinically driven features; a CatBoost classifier reaches a mean ROC AUC of 0.81 in the 4-class RANO response prediction task
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06511

### 3. EMedNeXt: An Enhanced Brain Tumor Segmentation Framework for Sub-Saharan Africa Using MedNeXt V2 with Deep Supervision (Co-author)
Jaheen, A., Elsayed, A., Kim, D., Tikhonov, D., Scatolin, M., Banerjee, M., Ji, Q., Salem, M., Wang, H., Hashmi, S., & Yaqub, M. (2026). In *Segmentation, Classification, and Synthesis for Brain Tumors and Traumatic Brain Injuries* (MICCAI 2025 / BraTS-Lighthouse), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16376, pp. 224-236. Springer, Cham.

- Enhanced MedNeXt V2 framework with deep supervision for robust glioma segmentation in sub-Saharan Africa; average LesionWise DSC of 0.897 on the hidden validation set
- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-16365-3_21
- Code: https://github.com/BioMedIA-MBZUAI/EMedNeXt-BraTS-SSA-2025

### 4. MISFIT: Modality Inference via Style Fusion and Invertible Translation for Cross-Modality Synthesis of 3D MRI Volumes (Co-author)
Banerjee, M., Ji, Q., Hashmi, S., Elsayed, A., Tikhonov, D., Scatolin, M. F., Jaheen, A., Kim, D., Wang, H., Salem, M., & Yaqub, M. (2026). In *Segmentation, Classification, and Synthesis for Brain Tumors and Traumatic Brain Injuries* (MICCAI 2025 / BraTS-Lighthouse), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16377, pp. 42-53. Springer, Cham.

- Two-stage generative framework for 3D brain MRI synthesis operating entirely in the wavelet domain (conditional wavelet diffusion with CAFF and Multi-Switchable SPADE), for the BraSyn task
- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-16370-7_4
- Code: https://github.com/mohrsalt/MISFIT

**Additional research:** automatic Knowledge Graph generation and Graph-RAG techniques (Instituto Kunumi, 2025-2026).

## Awards & Honors

### 2nd Place (Silver Medal), Itaú Asset Quant AI Challenge 2025
Itaú Asset Management | Dec 2025

- 2nd place out of **nearly 1,000 teams and 2,500+ participants** in Brazil's largest challenge for undergraduate students, which also featured Brazilian competitors from top global institutions (MIT, Stanford, Berkeley)
- Strategy developed: **KernelNet**, a market-neutral algorithmic trading strategy that generalizes pairs trading by replacing static correlations with nonlinear causality networks
- Performance: **Sharpe Ratio of 1.29** and **54.85% annualized return** (vs the benchmark's 22.78%), demonstrating robustness across different market regimes

## Application-Ready Material

*Written in first person, in my own voice, so it can be pasted directly into application forms.*

### Motivation (short, ~100 words)

What drives me is simple: building products that people love using and that make their lives a bit better. The technology is a means; the point is the person on the other side. I chose Computer Engineering because programming is the highest-leverage way I know to reach many people with real solutions, and every step since (LLM research, medical AI in Abu Dhabi, engineering at Latin America's largest AI startup, AI systems at a VC in San Francisco) has been picked for two things: learning fast and working with people I genuinely admire. Long term, I want to build products that carry my own signature, at an early-stage startup or by founding my own.

### Motivation (long version)

I won't pretend there was a lightning-bolt moment. I got into AI gradually: it sounded like the future, I took a first research opportunity at Semantix, and one door opened the next. What kept me, though, had nothing to do with hype. It was discovering the feeling of someone actually using something I built.

I got the first taste at Hyundai, where a model I developed was adopted by the team and people were genuinely happy with it. But the moment it really clicked was at Enter, Latin America's largest AI startup, where my role was closer to end-to-end software engineering than to research. I built a report generation tool, and when people started generating reports with it and telling me how much they loved it, I understood exactly what I want from my career. That feedback loop, someone's day getting easier because of something I shipped, is the thing I chase.

That is also why I am more focused on impact than on the technology behind it. I chose Computer Engineering over other majors because programming lets me reach more people and build solutions that help more of them. And it is why the startup path feels like a natural conclusion rather than a leap: a good startup is, at its core, solving a big problem that lots of people have. I want to build things that carry my face and my feel, and that level of ownership only exists with real independence, at an early-stage startup or founding my own.

Research and teaching both fit into this picture, each in its own way. Research is a powerful means to that end: at MBZUAI I co-authored three papers and my team won the Best Team Award, and I valued it precisely because it creates new ways of generating value for people. Teaching is something I genuinely love: I learn the most when I explain, which is why I taught a voluntary Python course at my former school, coordinated a 40-person team for Unicamp's largest outreach event, and keep giving talks that help Brazilian students access international opportunities.

I have a special feeling for Brazil, but I like helping people regardless of geography. And at this stage of my career, I optimize for exactly two things when choosing where to go: working with people I genuinely admire, who have done work I respect, and maximizing how fast I learn. Everything else is secondary.

### What drives me, ranked (for "what motivates you" questions)

1. **People using what I build.** Products that solve real problems and make lives better; the user's reaction is the reward
2. **Teaching and community.** I love teaching, and explaining a concept is when I learn it best
3. **Shipping production systems.** I enjoy the craft, but the pleasure is not the shipping itself; it is what happens after, when people use it
4. **Research novelty.** An awesome way of generating value for people, and a means to an end rather than the end itself
5. **Measurable business impact.** Useful evidence that something works, but not what gets me up in the morning

### Why startups and independence

- A good startup is solving a big problem that lots of people have, which is exactly what I want my career to be about
- I want to build things with my own signature, "my face and my feel," and that requires the independence found at early-stage startups or in founding my own
- I am not dogmatic about founding first: joining an exceptional early-stage team as an early employee is an open door

### How I choose opportunities (early career)

- **People:** working with genuinely admirable people who have done work I respect
- **Learning:** maximizing learning speed
- Everything else (prestige, compensation, geography) is currently secondary

### Career goals

- **Short term:** build products end to end alongside people I admire, at the intersection of AI and product engineering, learning as fast as possible
- **Medium term:** take real ownership of products in high-independence environments (early-stage startups, founder programs)
- **Long term:** found a company whose products make many people's lives better

### Signature stories (for behavioral questions)

- **Product impact (the "click" moment):** at Enter, built a report generation tool end to end; hearing users' feedback as they adopted it and loved it crystallized why I do this work
- **Leadership at scale:** as Projects Coordinator of Unicamp Portas Abertas (50,000+ visitors yearly), selected and coordinated a 40-person team based on project quality
- **Technical ownership:** at Enter, transformed a localized script into a resilient, distributed, production-grade pipeline (FastAPI, Hatchet, React, LLMs) processing thousands of judicial decisions
- **Performing under pressure:** at MBZUAI, delivered a complete 3D medical imaging pipeline in one summer, served as a final presenter, co-authored 3 papers, and won Best Team among 15 groups
- **Building from zero, fast:** at IE University, led the technical build of a two-sided AI assessment prototype in two weeks, reaching the Demo Day finals (top 3 of 15)
- **Competitive excellence:** designed KernelNet (Sharpe 1.29, 54.85% annualized return) and placed 2nd among ~1,000 teams in the Itaú Quant AI Challenge
- **Giving back:** taught a voluntary Python course at my former high school; led the "Pauta de Comunidade" session at Fundação Estudar's 2026 Onboarding
- **Failure and course correction:** at Enter, coming from an ML/research background into a software engineering role and pressured to ship fast, I over-delegated technical decisions to AI coding tools. When my boss asked me to explain my own architecture, I couldn't. From that day on, I own every technical decision deeply and use AI as leverage, never as a substitute for understanding
- **"Bring the cake half-baked":** after arriving at an architecture discussion with only ideas, my boss taught me to always bring a working first version to the table. I now make every discussion tangible: a v1 to react to, instead of abstractions to debate

### Logistics for application forms

- **Expected graduation:** December 2027 (B.Sc. Computer Engineering, Unicamp)
- **Citizenship / work authorization:** Brazilian and Italian (EU passport, eligible to work in the EU without sponsorship)
- **Languages:** Portuguese (native), English (fluent, EF SET C2)
- **Location:** Campinas, Brazil; open to international relocation
- **Availability:** internships during Brazilian summer (Dec-Feb) and mid-year breaks; full time after graduation
